subsystems.name: Quantum key distribution (QKD) link
subsystems.role: distributes symmetric keys whose secrecy rests on physics rather than on computational hardness.

subsystems.name: Quantum random number generator
subsystems.role: produces the unpredictable entropy that seeds keys, tokens and session identifiers.

subsystems.name: Post-quantum cryptography (PQC) layer
subsystems.role: protects credentials and signatures against future quantum computers without needing new hardware.

subsystems.name: Identity provider and credential store
subsystems.role: the classical layer that actually issues, revokes and validates identities.

subsystems.name: Key management and delivery
subsystems.role: moves quantum-derived keys from the link to the applications that need them.

subsystems.name: Quantum authentication primitives
subsystems.role: research-stage protocols that authenticate a party using quantum states or signatures.

buildSteps.title: Set the threat model
buildSteps.detail: Decide which identities need protection from 'harvest now, decrypt later' attacks, where keys must survive 10–20 years, and which links are short enough for fibre QKD.

buildSteps.title: Inventory credentials and protocols
buildSteps.detail: Catalogue every certificate, key, token format and signature algorithm across the identity estate, including long-lived code-signing and root certificates.

buildSteps.title: Roll out post-quantum cryptography first
buildSteps.detail: Swap key exchange and signatures to standardised PQC algorithms, deployed hybrid with existing ones so a break in either does not expose traffic. This needs no quantum hardware.

buildSteps.title: Install quantum entropy
buildSteps.detail: Replace or supplement software random number generators with quantum random number generators feeding the key management system.

buildSteps.title: Build QKD links
buildSteps.detail: Install point-to-point optical links between sites that matter — typically data centres, not individual users — and calibrate detectors for the loss of the fibre run.

buildSteps.title: Relay keys across the network
buildSteps.detail: For links beyond a few hundred kilometres, chain trusted nodes and a key management layer to carry keys end to end.

buildSteps.title: Wire into the identity provider
buildSteps.detail: Use a standard key-delivery interface so the authentication server fetches fresh symmetric keys without changes to application code.

buildSteps.title: Add quantum authentication where proven
buildSteps.detail: Layer quantum digital signature or token schemes only where their hardware and security proofs are mature enough for production.

buildSteps.title: Operate, rotate and audit
buildSteps.detail: Continuous key rotation, detector health monitoring, and independent audit of both the quantum and classical halves of the system.

prerequisites.why: commercial metro-scale systems exist, but distance is limited by fibre loss and detectors are costly and delicate.
NIST finalised ML-KEM, ML-DSA and SLH-DSA in 2024, giving an available alternative that needs no quantum link.
compact devices supply the entropy that quantum-derived keys depend on.
without them, keys cannot cross continents without trusted intermediate nodes that could in principle be subverted.
proposed protocols are insecure or impractical without long-term quantum memory and near-perfect detectors.

pathway.milestone: PQC migration in TLS, VPNs and certificate authorities, plus metro QKD testbeds
pathway.unlocks: identities that survive a future quantum computer; quantum links where fibre allows.

pathway.milestone: hybrid PQC-plus-QKD backbones between data centres and national quantum networks
pathway.unlocks: physical-layer key secrecy for the highest-value authentication traffic.

pathway.milestone: quantum repeaters and entanglement-based links in the laboratory
pathway.unlocks: key distribution over thousands of kilometres without trusting intermediate nodes.
identity proofs whose security does not depend on trusting the hardware vendor.
